title: Ever Walk into a Room and Forget What You Needed?

cues.text: You enter your living room, then pause.
cues.en: You enter your living room, then pause.
cues.zh: 你走進客廳，卻突然停了下來。

cues.text: You feel your mission’s momentum— but its aim is suddenly lost.
cues.en: You feel your mission’s momentum— but its aim is suddenly lost.
cues.zh: 你知道自己要去做某件事－－ 卻突然想不起目標為何。

cues.text: So, what just happened? And why does it keep happening?
cues.en: So, what just happened? And why does it keep happening?
cues.zh: 所以剛剛是怎麼回事？ 為什麼這種現象會一再發生？

cues.text: Well, you’re not alone;
cues.en: Well, you’re not alone;
cues.zh: 嗯，不只有你會這樣，

cues.text: this is actually a common phenomenon scientists have termed the doorway effect.
cues.en: this is actually a common phenomenon scientists have termed the doorway effect.
cues.zh: 這個現象很常見， 科學家把它稱為「門口效應」。

cues.text: According to psychological models,
cues.en: According to psychological models,
cues.zh: 根據心理學模型，

cues.text: our brains parse life’s continuous flow of time and activity into distinct events.
cues.en: our brains parse life’s continuous flow of time and activity into distinct events.
cues.zh: 我們的大腦會將生活中連續的時間 和活動劃分為一個一個的獨立事件。

cues.text: As a situation unfolds, the brain develops a working model of the event.
cues.en: As a situation unfolds, the brain develops a working model of the event.
cues.zh: 當某個事件發生時，大腦會針對 這個事件建立一個暫時的理解模型。

cues.text: It likely does this by employing its default mode network,
cues.en: It likely does this by employing its default mode network,
cues.zh: 它很可能是透過「預設 模式網路」來完成這件事，

cues.text: the brain regions that work together
cues.en: the brain regions that work together
cues.zh: 也就是由多個腦區共同運作、 負責休息時思考活動的神經網路。

cues.text: to accomplish many resting thought processes.
cues.en: to accomplish many resting thought processes.
cues.zh: 也就是由多個腦區共同運作、 負責休息時思考活動的神經網路。

cues.text: Then, when there's a big enough change,
cues.en: Then, when there's a big enough change,
cues.zh: 接著，當情境出現足夠大的變化時，

cues.text: the brain is thought to identify an event boundary,
cues.en: the brain is thought to identify an event boundary,
cues.zh: 大腦可能會辨識出 一個「事件邊界」。

cues.text: at which point it stores the prior event model,
cues.en: at which point it stores the prior event model,
cues.zh: 此時，大腦會儲存先前的事件模型，

cues.text: and begins developing a new working model.
cues.en: and begins developing a new working model.
cues.zh: 並開始建立新的暫時理解模型。

cues.text: During this switch, called an event update,
cues.en: During this switch, called an event update,
cues.zh: 這個切換時期稱為「事件更新」，

cues.text: parts of the default mode network
cues.en: parts of the default mode network
cues.zh: 此時，預設模式網路的某些部分

cues.text: seem to interact with the memory-storing hippocampus,
cues.en: seem to interact with the memory-storing hippocampus,
cues.zh: 似乎會與負責儲存記憶的 海馬迴產生互動，

cues.text: perhaps transporting the experience into longer-term memory.
cues.en: perhaps transporting the experience into longer-term memory.
cues.zh: 也許是將這段經歷傳輸到 更長期的記憶中。

cues.text: In the process, the brain clears its short-term memory,
cues.en: In the process, the brain clears its short-term memory,
cues.zh: 在此過程中，大腦 會清除其短期記憶，

cues.text: making room for the new information that’s already pouring in.
cues.en: making room for the new information that’s already pouring in.
cues.zh: 為已經不斷湧入的新資訊騰出空間。

cues.text: But sometimes that can be stuff you weren't quite done with.
cues.en: But sometimes that can be stuff you weren't quite done with.
cues.zh: 但有時候，那些被清除的資訊， 可能正是你還沒做完的事情。

cues.text: It’s still not fully clear if the doorway effect,
cues.en: It’s still not fully clear if the doorway effect,
cues.zh: 目前我們還不完全清楚， 門口效應

cues.text: also called the location updating effect,
cues.en: also called the location updating effect,
cues.zh: （也稱為「位置更新效應」）

cues.text: befalls some people more than others.
cues.en: befalls some people more than others.
cues.zh: 是否比較容易發生在某些人身上。

cues.text: But one study found that age had very little bearing.
cues.en: But one study found that age had very little bearing.
cues.zh: 但有一項研究發現， 年齡和此效應的關係不大。

cues.text: Scientists are working to better understand the phenomenon
cues.en: Scientists are working to better understand the phenomenon
cues.zh: 科學家還在努力 進一步瞭解這種現象，

cues.text: by pinpointing the conditions that trigger it,
cues.en: by pinpointing the conditions that trigger it,
cues.zh: 試圖找出究竟是什麼條件會觸發它，

cues.text: which, yes, includes doorways, both physical and virtual.
cues.en: which, yes, includes doorways, both physical and virtual.
cues.zh: 而答案確實包括「門口」—— 無論是實體的、還是虛擬的門口。

cues.text: In one study, college students in real and virtual spaces
cues.en: In one study, college students in real and virtual spaces
cues.zh: 有一項研究請大學生 在實體和虛擬空間中

cues.text: were asked to pick up objects, walk set distances carrying them out of view,
cues.en: were asked to pick up objects, walk set distances carrying them out of view,
cues.zh: 拿起某些物品，走一段指定的距離， 將物品放到視線之外，

cues.text: then try to recall what they were holding.
cues.en: then try to recall what they were holding.
cues.zh: 接著再嘗試回想剛才拿的是什麼。

cues.text: Time and distance remained constant, but some traveled through a doorway.
cues.en: Time and distance remained constant, but some traveled through a doorway.
cues.zh: 大家走的時間和距離都一樣， 但有些人的路線會穿過門口。

cues.text: Those who did tended to respond slower and be more likely to forget.
cues.en: Those who did tended to respond slower and be more likely to forget.
cues.zh: 有穿過門口的人通常反應會比較慢， 且比較有可能想不起來。

cues.text: And passing through multiple doorways
cues.en: And passing through multiple doorways
cues.zh: 而且，穿過多道門

cues.text: seems to worsen the memory-thwarting effect.
cues.en: seems to worsen the memory-thwarting effect.
cues.zh: 似乎會讓這種妨礙記憶的 效果更加明顯。

cues.text: It's also not helped by multitasking.
cues.en: It's also not helped by multitasking.
cues.zh: 就算一心多用也沒幫助。

cues.text: In another VR experiment,
cues.en: In another VR experiment,
cues.zh: 在另一項虛擬實境的實驗中，

cues.text: participants were first asked to memorize the colors and shapes
cues.en: participants were first asked to memorize the colors and shapes
cues.zh: 受試者先被要求記住 不同物品的顏色和形狀。

cues.text: of different objects.
cues.en: of different objects.
cues.zh: 接著，有些人在同一個房間中移動， 有些人則進入另一個房間。

cues.text: Then, some moved across the same room while others entered another.
cues.en: Then, some moved across the same room while others entered another.
cues.zh: 接著，有些人在同一個房間中移動， 有些人則進入另一個房間。

cues.text: When they were asked to also complete a counting task,
cues.en: When they were asked to also complete a counting task,
cues.zh: 同時他們也被要求要完成 一項計數工作，

cues.text: those who traveled through the doorway had a harder time
cues.en: those who traveled through the doorway had a harder time
cues.zh: 那些穿過門的人 更難回想起原本的物品。

cues.text: recalling the original objects.
cues.en: recalling the original objects.
cues.zh: 穿過門時受到的幹擾，

cues.text: Moving through the doorway distracted seemed to somehow overload their memory.
cues.en: Moving through the doorway distracted seemed to somehow overload their memory.
cues.zh: 穿過門時受到的幹擾，

cues.text: But the effect plagues people beyond literal doorways.
cues.en: But the effect plagues people beyond literal doorways.
cues.zh: 但並非只有穿過門口時， 人才會受到這種效應影響。

cues.text: Looking through clear walls into adjacent rooms also appears to do the trick.
cues.en: Looking through clear walls into adjacent rooms also appears to do the trick.
cues.zh: 從透明的牆看隔壁的房間 似乎也有同樣的效果。

cues.text: And really, whatever triggers an event update is thought to do the same:
cues.en: And really, whatever triggers an event update is thought to do the same:
cues.zh: 其實，只要能觸發事件更新， 就會產生同樣的效果，

cues.text: an alarm ringing; a friend changing the subject;
cues.en: an alarm ringing; a friend changing the subject;
cues.zh: 比如：鬧鐘響起、朋友改變話題，

cues.text: or a shift in location, time, motivation, or computer tab.
cues.en: or a shift in location, time, motivation, or computer tab.
cues.zh: 或是地點、時間、動機的改變， 或電腦分頁的切換。

cues.text: Likewise, when people come upon an event boundary while reading stories,
cues.en: Likewise, when people come upon an event boundary while reading stories,
cues.zh: 同樣地，當人們閱讀故事時 遇到「事件邊界」，

cues.text: like a sentence describing a considerable time jump,
cues.en: like a sentence describing a considerable time jump,
cues.zh: 比如讀到某個句子 描述時間大幅跳躍，

cues.text: researchers have observed that their reading speed may slow,
cues.en: researchers have observed that their reading speed may slow,
cues.zh: 研究人員觀察發現此時 讀者的閱讀速度會慢下來，

cues.text: their neural activity increases,
cues.en: their neural activity increases,
cues.zh: 神經活動也會增加，

cues.text: and they have more difficulty answering questions
cues.en: and they have more difficulty answering questions
cues.zh: 若問他們故事中的角色剛才 在做什麼，他們得花更多心力回想。

cues.text: about what a character was just doing.
cues.en: about what a character was just doing.
cues.zh: 但事件更新不見得 一定會造成這種現象。

cues.text: But this isn't always the case with event updating.
cues.en: But this isn't always the case with event updating.
cues.zh: 但事件更新不見得 一定會造成這種現象。

cues.text: In certain circumstances, doorways actually seem to aid memory.
cues.en: In certain circumstances, doorways actually seem to aid memory.
cues.zh: 在某些情況下， 門口似乎還有助記憶。

cues.text: In one study, participants were given lists of words,
cues.en: In one study, participants were given lists of words,
cues.zh: 在一項研究中，研究人員 會給受試者一張字詞清單，

cues.text: and in between them,
cues.en: and in between them,
cues.zh: 請他們在房間中四處移動或進入 另一個房間，再給他們下一張清單。

cues.text: they either moved spots within one room or walked into another.
cues.en: they either moved spots within one room or walked into another.
cues.zh: 請他們在房間中四處移動或進入 另一個房間，再給他們下一張清單。

cues.text: Those who switched rooms wound up recalling the words more faithfully.
cues.en: Those who switched rooms wound up recalling the words more faithfully.
cues.zh: 最後，有換房間的人 在回想字詞方面的表現更佳。

cues.text: The key difference in a doorway’s ability to strengthen versus muddle memory
cues.en: The key difference in a doorway’s ability to strengthen versus muddle memory
cues.zh: 門口到底會強化記憶 或是擾亂記憶，關鍵的差別

cues.text: might be the act of separating information into discrete events
cues.en: might be the act of separating information into discrete events
cues.zh: 可能在於是否把資訊 拆分成一個個獨立事件，

cues.text: versus sharing it among multiple.
cues.en: versus sharing it among multiple.
cues.zh: 而不是讓資訊全部混在一起。

cues.text: This may result in clearer compartmentalization
cues.en: This may result in clearer compartmentalization
cues.zh: 前者可能會讓資訊區隔更清楚明確，

cues.text: that helps reduce competition and interference
cues.en: that helps reduce competition and interference
cues.zh: 在試圖回想資訊時，就有助於減少 其他不相關資訊浮現及幹擾的狀況。

cues.text: when trying to recall the information.
cues.en: when trying to recall the information.
cues.zh: 通常，大腦會透過事件更新 來適應新的情境。

cues.text: Generally, event updating is the brain attempting to adapt to new situations.
cues.en: Generally, event updating is the brain attempting to adapt to new situations.
cues.zh: 通常，大腦會透過事件更新 來適應新的情境。

cues.text: But the doorway side effect can be disorienting.
cues.en: But the doorway side effect can be disorienting.
cues.zh: 但門口效應的副作用 有時會讓人混亂。

cues.text: So, how can we best pick our train of thought back up?
cues.en: So, how can we best pick our train of thought back up?
cues.zh: 那麼，若想把思考脈絡找回來， 最好的方法是什麼？

cues.text: Thankfully, the confusion tends to resolve on its own.
cues.en: Thankfully, the confusion tends to resolve on its own.
cues.zh: 好在，這種混亂通常會自動理清。

cues.text: But retracing your steps may help jog your memory.
cues.en: But retracing your steps may help jog your memory.
cues.zh: 但回想一遍先前做過的事 可能有助於喚回記憶。

cues.text: And people have also suggested that attempts
cues.en: And people have also suggested that attempts
cues.zh: 也有人指出，刻意預防 門口效應也有幫助，

cues.text: at deliberately preventing the doorway effect can help,
cues.en: at deliberately preventing the doorway effect can help,
cues.zh: 也有人指出，刻意預防 門口效應也有幫助，

cues.text: consciously keeping their goal in mind— perhaps repeating it verbally.
cues.en: consciously keeping their goal in mind— perhaps repeating it verbally.
cues.zh: 比如，有意識地去記住目標－－ 也許口頭上不斷重覆唸出來。

cues.text: Really, whatever helps you stay caught up so your head doesn’t get ahead of you.
cues.en: Really, whatever helps you stay caught up so your head doesn’t get ahead of you.
cues.zh: 其實大凡能讓你持續跟上思緒，不讓 你的大腦跑得比你快的方式都行。
